newsitem.title: INDONESIA: US rights official says Indonesia trip fruitful.
newsitem.headline: US rights official says Indonesia trip fruitful.

text.p: A top U.S. human rights official said on Friday his visit this week to East Timor had been fruitful and had underlined the urgency of dialogue over the troubled territory.
"I had a very productive five-day visit to Indonesia," John Shattuck, assistant secretary of state for democracy, human rights and labour, told reporters after leaving East Timor.
"A very effective and productive dialogue has taken place on human rights. It is a positive result of the visit," he said at Bali's Denpasar airport.
Shattuck arrived in Jakarta last Sunday and had talks with Foreign Minister Ali Alatas before flying to the East Timorese capital of Dili on Thursday for a 24-hour visit.
"I had a very fruitful visit in East Timor which stresses the urgency of the dialogue that is being promoted under the auspices of the U.N. secretary-general (Kofi Annan)," he said.
Indonesia has come under fire in the United States over its human rights record, especially on East Timor.

In Dili, Shattuck met Nobel Peace prize winner Bishop Carlos Belo, the governor Abilio Soares, the Indonesian military chief, the rector of the University of East Timor and a local editor and parliamentary representative from the territory.
The U.N. chief's new special assistant for East Timor, Jamsheed Marker, is also in Indonesia on a familiarisation visit and is due to visit Dili this weekend.
Indonesia invaded East Timor with tacit Western backing in December 1975 after civil war broke out following the withdrawal of Portuguese colonial authorities.
Indonesia incorporated the territory as its 27th province the following July in a move not recognised by the United Nations.

Marker visited Lisbon earlier this month and said he hoped for a speedy resumption of U.N.-sponsored talks between Indonesia and Portugal to reach an internationally acceptable solution for the future of East Timor.
The bilateral talks have dragged on for nearly 15 years without resolution.

Shattuck, on his arrival in Dili on Thursday, said the purpose of his visit to the territory "is to emphasise the importance the United States places on positive discussion under the auspices of the U.N. secretary-general on the issue of East Timor".
During his stop in Denpasar before flying to Cambodia later on Friday, Shattuck thanked the Indonesian government for arranging for him to meet dissident labour leader Muchtar Pakpahan.
Pakpahan, on trial on subversion charges that carry a possible death sentence, was taken to hospital for a biopsy on a tumour in his right lung. The results of the tests have still to be announced.
Shattuck said the visit gave him "the opportunity to stress the urgency of his receiving medical treatment".
